::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
Grew out of the 2018 SMIC–Shaoxing JV (中芯绍兴/中芯集成, renamed 芯联集成 on its 2022 STAR listing); today China's leading automotive power-semiconductor foundry — #1 Chinese SiC device maker by 2025 Yole ranking, in the global top-5 MEMS foundries — with 2025 output of 2.51 million 8-inch-equivalent wafers (+24.7%). Phase 3 (12-inch mixed-signal, ¥22.2 billion total, 100,000 wafers/month planned) is ramping from ~30,000/month; Phase 4 (¥20 billion, 50,000 wafers/month for 40/28nm MCU, 90/55nm BCD/DrMOS and 55nm silicon photonics) was announced June 2026.
:::

**Chinese name:** 芯联集成电路制造股份有限公司 (Xīnlián Jíchéng Diànlù Zhìzào Gǔfèn Yǒuxiàn Gōngsī)

## What does this facility make?

Car-grade IGBT/MOSFET and SiC MOSFET chips, MEMS sensors, analog/BCD and mixed-signal chips for EVs, industrial, renewables and AI-server power/optical I/O.

## Why does it matter?

Its 8-inch SiC line was China's first (engineering wafers April 2024, mass production confirmed August 2025) — SiC vehicle main-drive modules are the single highest-value target of China's power-semi push, and UnitedNova operates the scaled foundry slot for it. No controlling shareholder: largest holders Yuecheng Fund (local state) 13.74% and SMIC Holdings 11.85%.

## Project Timeline

- **Dec 2018** — Founded as the SMIC–Shaoxing joint venture (中芯绍兴)
- **Apr 2024** — China's first 8-inch SiC line produces engineering wafers
- **Aug 2025** — 8-inch SiC confirmed in mass production; Phase 3 12-inch line at ~30,000 wafers/month of planned 100,000
- **Jun 2026** — ¥20 billion Phase 4 JV announced — 50,000 wafers/month 12-inch for 40/28nm MCU, BCD/DrMOS and 55nm silicon photonics
